notes: The sources the game draws on and acknowledges: the pause menu's Credits screen (game/scripts/ui/hud.gd) shows every entry, in this order. This file is the only list; no scene or script repeats it.

An entry: id, title, credit (the line to show; several works one a line, each shown after a bullet), licence and url (empty if none), required (true where the licence asks for the acknowledgement, false where it is a courtesy) and used_for. Optional: licence_file, a licence text that ships with the game and shows under the screen's Licences button (export_presets.cfg's include_filter must list it); engine, for Godot Engine, whose own licence and its third-party notices come from Engine.get_license_text(), get_copyright_info() and get_license_info(), also under Licences; loading_screen, a credit the loading screen shows too; folders, the project folders the entry covers.

game/tests/headless_credits_contract.gd fails when a folder under game/ or generated/ holds a licence or provenance file (LICENSE, LICENCE, COPYING, NOTICE, PROVENANCE, ATTRIBUTION, AUTHORS, CREDITS, OFL), fonts, sounds, videos or 3D models, image data under a name that isn't an image's (a PNG kept as .dat), or a file an export preset's include_filter adds, or sits directly in a vendor, addons or third_party folder, or is a folder under game/resources/ that holds images, and is listed neither in an entry's folders nor in own_work (the project's own, made here or supplied by the owner, which need no credit, each with what is recorded of how it was made). The match is exact: a folder never covers the folders inside it. It fails too when a listed folder is gone.

Not listed because nothing of them ships: reference photos and Street View (looked at, never in the game), the Kenney Nature Kit and the NAIP-placed placeholder vegetation (both removed), and the npm packages and tools that generate the world offline.

entries.title: OpenStreetMap
entries.used_for: The island's layout: its shoreline, roads, paths, parks and every building's footprint (August 2026 snapshot), and the coasts, bridges and waterfronts on the horizon.

entries.title: Godot Engine
entries.credit: This game uses Godot Engine, available under the MIT licence.
entries.used_for: The game engine. Its full licence, and the software by other authors it includes with their licences, are under Licences.

entries.title: Godot 4 Third Person Controller (touch controls)
entries.used_for: The touch screen's stick and buttons, and their art, adapted. Its licence is under Licences.

entries.title: USGS 3D Elevation Program
entries.credit: Elevation data: U.S. Geological Survey, 3D Elevation Program (3DEP)
entries.used_for: The height of the ground on Treasure Island and Yerba Buena Island (the 1 m elevation model of 2023).

entries.title: Aerial imagery
entries.credit: Source: Esri, Vantor, Earthstar Geographics, and the GIS User Community
entries.licence: Esri World Imagery terms of use
entries.used_for: Tree positions, Yerba Buena Island's plant cover and some ground and shoreline shapes were read from the aerial photo of 26 May 2026 (World Imagery Wayback). None of the imagery itself is in the game.

entries.title: Poly Haven
entries.credit: Textures from Poly Haven: clean_asphalt, concrete_pavement, concrete_floor_03, sparse_grass, plaster_grey_04 and bitumen
entries.used_for: Road asphalt, pavements and paved areas, the grass detail, wall plaster and flat roofs.

entries.title: Public art
entries.credit:
Point of Infinity by Hiroshi Sugimoto (Yerba Buena Island)
Canopy of Sky by Ned Kahn (Cityside Park)
entries.used_for: Modelled after the real works, which stand on the islands.

entries.title: Murals
entries.credit:
Bulgaria in the USA by Oleg Gotchev (the handball courts at Ninth Street and Avenue D)
Rocky Purslane by Nathaniel J. Bice (Mersea restaurant, Treasure Island)
The mural on the north-northwest end wall of Building 201 (Island Cove Market, 800 Avenue I), Treasure Island; its artist is not established
entries.used_for: Painted reconstructions of the real murals, as game art rather than exact copies: Bulgaria in the USA and Rocky Purslane from photographs of them, Building 201's from a written description of photographs.
